parts: Vladmir Stasov claimed that what movement depicts a creature "clumsily running with crooked legs?" This E-flat minor movement follows its piece's first promenade.
Movements like "Gnomus" and "the Old Castle" depict Viktor Hartmann's artworks in this suite by Modest Mussorgsky.
Pictures at an Exhibition returns to an E-flat tonic for this last movement of the piece, which begins with a slow brass fanfare in Maurice Ravel's orchestration.

bonuses.leadin: This was the first theory to classify transition metal complexes as "high-spin" or "low-spin." For 10 points each:
parts: Name this theory that models the breaking of orbital degeneracy in transition metals due to the static electric field of surrounding anions.
Crystal field theory is most commonly applied to these orbitals, whose "z-squared" example is the only one without four lobes. Transition metals can store up to 10 electrons in these atomic orbitals.
Ligands higher on the spectrochemical series form lower-spin complexes; one of the highest ligands is this ion, equivalent to a nitrile group, that complexes with iron to form Prussian blue.

bonuses.leadin: This term originally referred to a fire safety device in theaters. For 10 points each:
parts: Give this term, whose first use in a political sense may have been in Vernon Lee’s 1915 book The Ballet of Nations. This term was popularized at a speech in Fulton, Missouri in 1946.
This politician gave the Iron Curtain speech at Fulton. This Prime Minister's other greatest hits include the "we shall fight on the beaches" speech during World War II.

A sculptor from this family named Gabriela designed a monument of a literal Iron Curtain for Fertőrákos ("FEHR-tuh-rah-kohsh"), Hungary. A much earlier member of this family adopted the motto A.E.I.O.U.

bonuses.leadin: In a story by this author, a wounded criminal is carried into town by his father, who asks him to listen for dogs barking. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this author of the story collection El llano en llamas who wrote a novel about Juan Preciado seeking his father, whose name contains the Spanish word for "wasteland."
Rulfo is an author from this country. Native author Octavio Paz wrote about this country in The Labyrinth of Solitude.
The public-domain website Ciudad Seva that hosts many of Rulfo's stories is named for a fictional town in this region. An author born in this region wrote the cross-genre Spanglish novel Yo-Yo Boing.

bonuses.leadin: The Isaac Potts House is often named for providing this service to George Washington at Valley Forge. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this service that Nathanael Greene oversaw while leading a corps of its namesake "masters." Providing this service for soldiers during peacetime is banned by the Third Amendment.
The Second Quartering Act was part of this set of laws that Thomas Gage oversaw, which also included the Port Act.

Continental soldiers scornfully coined the phrase "[this man's] quarter" after his dragoons massacred surrendering Americans at the Battle of Waxhaws. He commanded and sometimes names the British Legion.

bonuses.leadin: Guido Reni's homoerotic painting of Saint Sebastian in this position partially inspired Oscar Wilde's pseudonym of Sebastian Melmoth. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this position of figures who stand with most of their weight on one foot.

This artist, who chased an apprentice and lover to Ferrara when the latter left his studio, placed David in an exaggerated contrapposto for a bronze sculpture in which he stands on the head of Goliath.

Vasari wrote of how a painter from this city, who wrote many songs about his love of boys, acquired the nickname Il Sodoma. The Allegory of Good and Bad Government is a fresco series depicting this city's council.

bonuses.leadin: Infinite descent involves contradicting this theorem by showing that a falsehood would have to apply to arbitrarily many smaller numbers. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this theorem that is often conflated with the less general statement that every nonempty subset of N contains a least element.
N denotes this set, which can be defined as either the set of non-negative integers or of positive integers.

Work on the well-ordering theorem caused Ernst Zermelo to introduce this equivalent statement. This statement, which is the "C" in "ZFC," enables the creation of a set consisting of one element from each of infinitely many collections.

bonuses.leadin: Ivan Illich argued that industrial society's over-reliance on people in this profession causes harm through the process of iatrogenesis. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this profession whose ethical standards are upheld through the Hippocratic oath.

Illich's views disagree with those of this sociologist, whose concept of the "sick role" includes an obligation to visit doctors. This sociologist developed the AGIL paradigm in his book The Structure of Social Action.
According to Parsons, people in the "sick role" oxymoronically exhibit a "sanctioned" example of this type of behavior, which is categorized as the violation of social norms.

bonuses.leadin: In this tone poem, second violins and violas lead a metric modulation to a section in 2/4 time depicting a farmer's wedding. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this tone poem that begins in 6/8 time with the second flute playing a fragment of an E minor scale. One of its themes is based on the 17th-century madrigal "La Mantovana."
Die Moldau is part of this cycle of six tone poems by Bedřich Smetana depicting locations and events in modern-day Czechia.

The first tone poem in Má vlast, Vyšehrad ("vee-SHEH-rahd"), begins with a duet in which one of these instruments plays block chords while another plays arpeggios. This instrument's 47 strings are plucked with both hands.

bonuses.leadin: These diagrams are used to minimize the number of logic gates on hardware systems. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these diagrams consisting of Gray-coded truth tables that are used for manual implementation of the Quine–McCluskey algorithm. Grouping cells of these diagrams into implicants assists with Boolean minimization.
The number of terms in a minterm group of a Karnaugh map is one of these numbers. In binary, these numbers are represented with precisely one digit set to one.
The Karnaugh map representing this function is a two-by-two grid with only one zero cell, since this Boolean function asserts true when one or both of its inputs are true.

bonuses.leadin: Frances Gage's recording of this speech inaccurately rendered it in dialect and added the phrase for which it is commonly titled. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this speech, whose speaker declared, "I have plowed and reaped and husked and chopped and mowed, and can any man do more than that?"
This abolitionist speaker gave the speech "Ain't I a Woman?"

Truth corresponded with this author of An Appeal in Favor of that Class of Americans Called Africans, who is better known for writing “The Quadrooms” and the poem "Over the River and Through the Woods."

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following about coffeehouses, for 10 points each.
parts: The first coffeehouses were founded in this city, from which they spread rapidly throughout the Ottoman Empire and into Europe. Europeans mistakenly thought that steel with wavy patterns originated from this city.
Lloyd’s of London, a company now in this industry, was founded as a coffeehouse. Astronomer Edmund Halley developed the first table used in the "life" subfield of this industry.

This philosopher claimed that coffeehouses and salons were centers of "rational-critical debate" in early modern Europe. This philosopher attacked Ernst Nolte's "apologistic" history of the Nazi era in the Historikerstreit.

bonuses.leadin: The title curate magically keeps a whiskey bottle full during a weekend of drinking with the faithless priest Angwin in this author's novel Fludd. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this author, who described her Catholic school upbringing in Giving Up the Ghost. This author fictionalized a man who states the world is not run "from the castle walls, but from counting houses."
Hilary Mantel broke with literary tradition by her positive depiction of Thomas Cromwell in a historical trilogy starting with this novel.
In contrast to Cromwell, Wolf Hall negatively depicted Thomas More, the author of this 1516 political allegory about an ideal society.

bonuses.leadin: Description acceptable. A 2025 book by Yoni Appelbaum examines declining rates of this activity in the US. For 10 points each:
parts: "Golden handcuffs" of low mortgage interest rates are contributing to fewer Americans engaging in what activity, central to Zillow's business model?

In 2021, a Victorian house near this city's iconic Painted Ladies was moved to make room for an apartment complex. Zoning reforms were part of Mayor London Breed's efforts to alleviate this city's housing crisis.
Constructing more housing is part of an "agenda" of this name. A 2025 book co-authored by Ezra Klein with this name demands "a liberalism that builds."

bonuses.leadin: This figure is forced to give up his right thumb in observance of guru·dakshina. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this prince of the Nishada tribe who claims to have learned archery from Dronacharya after studying for years from a statue of him.

Eklavya's prowess is discovered when he shoots multiple arrows in the mouth of a dog owned by these figures without killing it. The twin children of the Ashvins are part of this group, who are exiled after losing a rigged game of dice.
The story of Eklavya appears in this Hindu epic about the Kurukshetra War that contains the Bhagavad Gita.

bonuses.leadin: The temperature at which this process occurs is inversely proportional to molecular weight by the Flory–Fox equation. For 10 points each:
parts: Polymers in a material can experience conformational changes in finite time after undergoing what process? This process corresponds to a "step" in the plot of a signal during differential scanning calorimetry.
The glass transition causes an increase in a material's value of this quantity, the amount of energy it takes to raise a material's temperature by one degree.
Above the glass transition temperature, rubber elastomers maintain a solid structure due to these bonds between polymer chains.

bonuses.leadin: 1930s newsreels often failed to directly capture newsworthy events. For 10 points each:
parts: One exception was when a camera capturing routine footage of a mooring at Lakehurst, New Jersey, caught the fiery destruction of this zeppelin, named for a German field marshal.

A $5,000 bounty by Universal Newsreel to capture this event on camera went unclaimed. A failed attempt at this action began after Melvin Purvis lit his cigar outside the Biograph Theater in Chicago in 1934.
A newsreel series with this last word in its title often used dramatic reenactments. This word titles a publication founded in 1923 that Henry Luce published, in addition to Life.

bonuses.leadin: In antenna theory, this regime holds beyond a distance defined as either twice wavelength or twice dimension-squared over wavelength. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this regime in which the angular field distribution is independent of distance from the antenna. In this regime, diffraction is modeled as the result of in-phase plane waves.

Receiving antennae are contrasted with antennae that perform this process. This process, whose coefficient equals one minus the reflection coefficient, precedes power distribution in namesake "lines."
Power patterns of antennae are often given in this log-scale unit. This is the typical unit for the volume of sound.

bonuses.leadin: Description acceptable. In one play, two men who dress up as the spirits of Rape and Murder are killed by its title character before being subjected to this action. For 10 points each:
parts: Describe this action, which that character performs to desecrate the corpses of Demetrius and Chiron in revenge for their violent mutilation of his daughter Lavinia.
To write Titus Andronicus, Shakespeare likely drew from this Roman tragedian's play Thyestes, whose title character is fed pies made from his sons to avenge an affair with his brother's wife.
In the Victorian penny dreadful The String of Pearls, Mrs Lovett makes pies from the victims of this serial killer, the "Demon Barber of Fleet Street".

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about items falling on the heads of Ancient Greeks. For 10 points each:
parts: Draco died after being suffocated with the hats, shirts, and cloaks of his supporters in one of these locations. Many of Aeschylus' plays were performed at an Athenian one of these places.
Tarquinius Priscus, whose father's origin in this city prevented him from holding office in Etruria, had an eagle drop a cap on his head in Rome. Lucius Mummius Achaicus destroyed this city.
This Greek king was killed after an old woman dropped a roof tile on his head in Argos. This man, the first to use war elephants against Rome, defeated the Romans at Heraclea and Asculum.

bonuses.leadin: Ludwig Wittgenstein's Philosophical Investigations begins with this philosopher's account of learning language as a child. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this author who wrote about his conversion from Manichaeism to Christianity in his Confessions.
In De doctrina christiana, Augustine outlines an early theory of this field by contrasting "things" with the signs that represent them. This field is the study of how signs communicate meaning.

Augustine called lying sinful because it goes against language's purpose as a communicative medium in a work titled for this Greek word for "handbook," which also titles a work by the Stoic philosopher Epictetus ("EP-ick-TEE-tuss").

bonuses.leadin: After his bell towers were blamed for causing cracks in the facade of St. Peter's Basilica, this sculptor began, but never finished, the piece Truth Unveiled by Time. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Baroque sculptor of The Ecstasy of St. Teresa.

This Bernini artwork in St. Peter's Basilica required so much bronze that some was looted from the portico of the Pantheon. This large canopy covers the basilica's high altar and is covered in bees representing Urban VIII.

Though he fell out of favor with Innocent X, Bernini was commissioned by the Pamphili family for this sculpture in which an obelisk covered in hieroglyphs towers above gods of locations in South America and Asia.

bonuses.leadin: This month was traditionally the most popular time for hakawati performances. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this holy month that, in the 21st century, usually corresponds with a big increase in evening TV viewership for its namesake dramas. Jordan imposes fines for not observing a fast during this month.
Hakawati performances and Ramadan soaps would be watched following this fast-breaking meal.

Many retailers, especially those throughout Egypt and the Levant, decorate their stores with elaborate examples of these objects called fawanees during Ramadan. In another tradition, these objects often have riddles written on them during Cap Go Meh.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about dances named after their sounds, for 10 points each.
parts: Though originally named for a bagpipe, bal-musette dances are most frequently performed to this instrument. Polka and zydeco dances are done to concertinas and this bellow-like instrument with a keyboard.
This dance's name derives from the sound of shoes when performing a triple step. Like the mambo, this Cuban dance is derived from danzón.

In a dance similar to stepping, South African miners communicated with each other by slapping these specific clothing items. These rubber items inspired by Hessian examples were popularized by a British prime minister.

bonuses.leadin: Carlos Menem broke with this ideology by implementing free market reforms. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this political ideology centered around strong trade unions and anti-elite populism. The descamisados ("DESS-cah-mee-SAH-dose") supported this ideology's namesake leader, whose return from exile coincided with the Ezeiza ("eh-SAY-sa") Massacre.
Perón advocated for a system with this name that rejects communism and capitalism. In "Ur-Fascism," Umberto Eco analyzes an "International" movement of this name founded by Roberto Fiore.
Working class Argentinians supported Peron after the charitable efforts of this wife of his, who died in 1952. A first name is acceptable.

bonuses.leadin: The title character Fatima dies just after seeing her children during one of these events in the Balkan ballad Hasanaginica ("hah-sah-nah-gih-NITS-ah"). For 10 points each:
parts: The Croatian poet Michael Verancius celebrated one of what events by writing an epithalamion ("eh-pith-uh-LAY-mee-on")? In the lost poem Cypria ("COOP-ree-uh"), the Apple of Discord is thrown at one of these events.
Hasanaginica came to wider prominence through a translation by this German author, written shortly after this author's debut novel The Sorrows of Young Werther ("VER-tuh").
This author made a French translation of Hasanaginica in 1841. Zosia is engaged to the title character at the end of this poet's Polish national epic Pan Tadeusz ("tah-DAY-oosh").

bonuses.leadin: Pairs of these structures are distinguished by color in the "spectral" technique SKY. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these structures visualized by a karyotype, enabling the diagnosis of disorders of these structures like Down's syndrome.

Down's syndrome involves a third copy of chromosome 21, so it is in this broad class of disorders defined by aberrant chromosome counts. This type of disorder, which often arises from nondisjunction in the early embryo, is the leading genetic cause of miscarriage.
Tri·somies like Down's syndrome can arise from the retention of one of these cells in the egg. Oogenesis ("OH-oh-genesis") produces three of these small haploid cells.

bonuses.leadin: Exodus 31:14 states that a punishment for this sin is "that soul shall be cut off from among his people." For 10 points each:
parts: Name or describe this action that an unidentified man commits by gathering sticks in Numbers 15, causing him to be stoned by the congregation.
The next few verses of Numbers provide the Bible's first description of these "fringes in the borders of their garments." These tassels with a repetitive name adorn the tallit.

Wearing tzitzit is this type of Jewish "commandment" or "good deed," of which there are 613 in the Torah. The name of these acts are preceded by "bar" or "bat" in the name of the Jewish coming-of-age ceremony.
